about: Synthetic conformance streams for the WI portrait decoder of spec/wi-codec.md (revision 3). Each stream was generated by an encoder from made-up content (no card data, nothing derived from the public vectors) to reach decoder paths the six public vectors do not. Valid cases carry the scalars and checkpoint hashes of section 14, defined exactly as in wi-checkpoints.json. Failing cases carry expected_error, the canonical error of section 12: the first error condition met in reading order. Where the reference, which keeps running after an error, meets further conditions later, reference_error_sequence lists them in order; only the first is canonical. Expected values come from an instrumented copy of the reference reconstruction, and an independent implementation of the spec reproduces them. Every stream has the licence header shape except where a failing case says otherwise, and is at most 674 bytes except e1-size-675.
checkpoints: as in wi-checkpoints.json: C1_ll, C2_map, per level C3_upsampled, C4_coefficients, C5_reconstructed, then C6_sharpened, C7_raster, C8_portrait

errors.E1: header not the licence profile, or size outside 13..674
errors.E5: run count not exactly exhausted after the map
errors.canonical: the first condition met in reading order; a decoder may stop there (section 12)

coverage: Together the valid cases reach: skip 0 to 5; LL widths 0, 1, 3, 4 to 9, 12, 16, 17, 18 and 31 (offset kept to 8 bits); escape widths 0 to 10; both large-value leaves (256 in runs, 2048 in magnitudes); nested run extensions, and low symbols 255 and 256; empty and dense maps; Q = 0 and 255; 32-bit wrap-around in the LL values, in the run arithmetic, and in the upsampling at levels 4 and 3; the truncating divisions of 9.1 changing values; non-zero trailing bytes.
